newsitem.title: BRUNEI: South African president arrives in Brunei.
newsitem.headline: South African president arrives in Brunei.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela arrived on Monday in the tiny oil-rich country of Brunei, continuing a swing through Asia that began with a two-day visit to the Philippines over the weekend.

Mandela, accompanied by a 12-member delegation including his companion Graca Machel, was met in Brunei by Foreign Minister Prince Mohammad Bolkiah. Machel is the 51-year-old widow of former Mozambican president Somora Machel.
After inspecting a guard of honour mounted by the Royal Brunei Armed Forces, Mandela had an audience with the Sultan of Brunei which was followed by private discusssions.
The South African president said he is on a four-nation tour in the region to learn from its "Tiger" economies on how to raise the living conditions of his own people.
He has also said he is keen to deepen relations with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
Mandela made his first visit to Brunei in 1990.
Aides said Mandela would be relaxing during the Brunei visit and was scheduled to tour the country's popular tourist attraction, the water village, on Monday afternoon.
Mandela visits Malaysia and Singapore next before returning to South Africa.
